lessons.gloss: what set it off; the starting cause

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 起因

segments.text: 起因 — qǐyīn — "what set it off; the starting cause".
rúguǒ zhīdào le qǐyīn jiù néng jiějué wèntí — If we know what set it off, we can solve the problem.

起因 (qǐyīn) is built from 起 'to rise, to start' and 因 'a cause', both inherited from Middle Chinese, khiX and 'jin (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to rise' and 'to start' and the second 'to rest on' and 'to follow from'.
One more word for saying what would happen.

lessons.title: 原来 (yuánlái) — so (it turns out); as it turns out
lessons.gloss: so (it turns out); as it turns out

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for something to look forward to, then the Mandarin for what set it off.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: 原来

segments.text: 原来 — yuánlái — "so (it turns out); as it turns out".
原来你也在这儿 yuánlái nǐ yě zài zhèr — So you're here too!

The new character, in pieces: 原 (yuán) — ten strokes: the cliff, a bar and a long stroke falling to the left, as at the top of 愿; under it 白, five strokes, and 小, three strokes: 愿 without its heart. The next lesson puts it in your hand.

原来 (yuánlái) is built from 原 (yuán) and 来 'to come', both inherited from Middle Chinese, ngjwon and loj (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription). The dictionary glosses the first as wide flat land, a plain; the sense 'origin' is not given there, and how the pair came to mean 'as it turns out' is not settled.
One more word for saying what would happen.

blocks.title: Script — the cliff over 白 and 小

segments.text: 原 (yuán).
Three pieces: the cliff, then 白, then 小 under it. Count the pieces, not the strokes.
The cliff, two strokes: a bar, then a long stroke falling to the left down from its left end.
白, five strokes, under the cliff's arm: a short stroke falling to the left, a vertical, a bar that turns down, two short bars.
小, three strokes: a vertical that hooks to the left, a short stroke on its left, a dot on its right.
2 + 5 + 3 = ten, the first ten strokes of 愿.

lessons.title: dǎozhì — to result in something bad

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for what set it off, then the Mandarin for as it turns out.
dǎozhì — "to result in something bad".
rúguǒ bú zhùyì jiù huì dǎozhì shìgù — If you're careless, it will lead to an accident.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

dǎozhì is built from dǎo 'to lead' and zhì 'to bring to', both inherited from Middle Chinese, dawH and trijH (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to lead' and the second 'to arrive' and 'to send to'. The dipping tone of dǎo is not the regular outcome of dawH.
One more word for saying what would happen.

lessons.title: zàochéng — to cause damage or trouble

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for as it turns out, then the Mandarin for to result in something bad.
zàochéng — "to cause damage or trouble".
rúguǒ nǐ bù shuō jiù huì zàochéng wùhuì — If you don't say anything, it will cause a misunderstanding.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.
zàochéng is built from zào 'to make' and 成 'to complete', both inherited from Middle Chinese, dzawX and dzyeng (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to make'.
One more word for saying what would happen.

lessons.title: xiàoguǒ — the effect it has (how well it works)
lessons.gloss: the effect it has (how well it works)

segments.text: Before the new one: say the Mandarin for to result in something bad, then the Mandarin for to cause damage.
xiàoguǒ — "the effect it has (how well it works)".
yàoshi méiyǒu xiàoguǒ nǐ jiù huàn yí ge bànfǎ — If it doesn't work, try another way.
Its characters come later; for now it is a word for the ear.

xiàoguǒ is built from xiào and 果 'fruit', both inherited from Middle Chinese, haewH and kwaX (Guangyun, in Baxter's transcription), which glosses the first 'to imitate' and 'proven effect': what the effort bears.
One more word for saying what would happen.
